title: Sales enablement: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch deck, pricing & security FAQ
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference sales and pre-sales teams. It consolidates positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance and worked examples, two concise case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this as the single source of truth for customer-facing proposals, demos, and RFP responses.

Audience: AEs, SEs, solutions engineers, partnerships, and marketing.

Owner & maintenance cadence:
- Owner: Go-to-market (Enablement)
- Primary contact: Elena Martinez (elena@redwoodinference.com)
- Review cadence: Quarterly (content owner to schedule review 30 days before quarter-end)

1) Positioning & core messaging

Elevator pitch (30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable, economical, and flexible across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so engineering teams can ship LLM features with consistent latency, cost control, and enterprise-grade reliability.

Three core value props (customer-focused):
- Predictable performance at scale: SLA-backed dedicated capacity plus an optimized runtime (continuous batching, KV caching, quantization profiles) for low tail latency and consistent throughput.
- Cost- and developer-aware controls: Clear levers (batching, cache, model-variant routing, quantization) that reduce per-token unit economics without sacrificing quality.
- Flexible deployment modes: Hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and Private/VPC/on-prem packages for regulated and high-security workloads.

Message hierarchy (talk tracks by persona):
- Engineering / Platform: Focus on reproducible performance, runtime tuning, and observability hooks (token-level latency/cost). Reference the SDK, tracing, and rollout APIs for canaries/A-B tests.
- Product / Data Science: Emphasize model lifecycle features (version pinning, rollouts, automated rollback), integrated evals, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
- Security / Compliance: Highlight private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC/ISO evidence.

Examples: 2-line customer-friendly feature callouts
- "Reduce inference cost by 2–5x on chat workloads with our automatic prefix caching and batching recommendations."
- "Meet regional data residency and audit requirements using Private deployment with customer-managed KMS."

2) Competitive brief (one-pager summary + matrix)

Competitive positioning summary: Use this brief to quickly differentiate against the two most common competitive sets: managed LLM API providers (simplicity-first) and self-hosted inference runtimes (control-first).

Competitive matrix (high-level):

| Capability                       | Redwood Inference                        | Managed LLM API (simplicity-first) | Self-hosted runtime (control-first) |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Deployment modes                 | Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem)| Hosted only / limited dedicated    | Self-hosted only                    |
| SLAs & enterprise support        | SLA-backed Dedicated plans + Premium SLAs| Basic support tiers                 | Varies (customer-managed)           |
| Cost controls                    | Batching, KV caching, quantization guide | Limited tooling                    | Full control but heavy ops cost     |
| Observability                    | Token-level cost/latency, per-route logs | Request logs only                  | Depends on implementation           |
| PII & compliance                 | Private deployment + KMS/HSM integrations | Varies by provider                 | Customer responsibility             |
| Time to value                    | Fast via Hosted API + migration guides   | Very fast                          | Slow (build + ops)                  |

Quick rebuttals and talk tracks:
- If prospect says "We can self-host cheaper": acknowledge potential cost but highlight TCO: ops, reliability, and time-to-market. Offer a TCO checklist and propose a pilot with metrics tracking.
- If prospect says "We need simplicity": emphasize Hosted API for quick results and our pre-configured model catalog and SDKs.
- If prospect raises vendor lock-in: point to unified API and ability to run the same models/rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

3) Pitch Deck: recommended 12-slide outline (core deck for new prospects)

Slide 00: Title & logo (contact info, AE + SE names)
Slide 01: TL;DR value prop (2–3 bullets with quantified outcomes)
Slide 02: The problem (real-world latency / cost / reliability tradeoffs)
Slide 03: Redwood Inference solution overview (key differentiators)
Slide 04: How it works at a high level (serving runtime + smart routing + caching)
Slide 05: Deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) + when to choose each
Slide 06: Performance proof points (benchmarks: median latency, p95, throughput for common models)
Slide 07: Cost story (example unit economics and savings)
Slide 08: Security & compliance (KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO readiness)
Slide 09: Customer success (2 short case studies + logos)
Slide 10: Pilot proposal (timeline, success metrics, responsibilities)
Slide 11: Pricing overview & next steps (contacts, legal/PO info)

Pitch guidance (presentation tips):
- Start with the outcome the prospect cares about (latency, unit cost, time to market).
- For technical buyers, be prepared to deep dive into runtime architecture and observability dashboards.
- For procurement/security, open with Private deployment options and compliance evidence packet.

4) Pricing guidance & worked examples

Principles: be transparent, outcome-oriented, and provide a clear path from trial to commit. Pricing components:
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation, per-embedding unit) with free credits for evaluation.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved GPU capacity (committed throughput tiers) + optional burst capacity.
- Private: platform licensing + support/operational fees.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, premium SLA, compliance package.

Worked example: mid-market chat product (estimates)
- Assumptions: 50M tokens/month, 80% generation, 20% embeddings, typical chat model (context 2k tokens average)
- Hosted example pricing: 50M tokens * $0.0004/token = $20k/month (illustrative) + 200k embeddings * $0.002 = $400/month
- Dedicated example: Reserved Tier C (8 A100-equivalent GPUs) = $18k/month committed + 10% burst usage billed at on-demand rate.

Pricing JSON snippet (shareable with AEs when creating proposals):
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-2k",
  "deployment": "dedicated",
  "reserved_gpus": "8",
  "monthly_commit_usd": "18000",
  "burst_allowance_pct": "10",
  "support_tier": "enterprise"
}

Discounting policy (high-level):
- Standard discounts available for 12+ month commitments and higher volume tiers.
- For strategic enterprise deals, work with Sales Ops for SKU bundling (Private + Dedicated + Compliance).

Quote timeline SLA: Sales ops to produce a formal quote within 48 business hours of signed LOI request; SE to deliver sizing + pilot plan within 5 business days.

5) Case studies (concise one-page summaries)

Case study A — Fintech aggregator (Mid-market)
- Customer problem: Real-time summarization and insight extraction for customer support; prior infra had p95 latency spikes > 1.5s causing poor UX.
- Solution: Redwood Hosted API with KV prefix caching and token-aware batching, plus model pinning to a quantized variant.
- Outcome (30-day pilot): p95 latency reduced from 1.5s to 420ms; inference cost reduced by 48% vs baseline; error rate for hallucinated summaries decreased by 12% (measured on a targeted eval set).
- Owner: Customer Success (Ravi Shah)

Case study B — Regulated healthcare customer (Enterprise)
- Customer problem: Must meet data residency and KMS-backed encryption requirements; required on-prem capabilities and audit evidence.
- Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, integrated with their HSM (AWS CloudHSM) and audit log forwarding to SIEM.
- Outcome: Deployment completed in 8 weeks; passed customer SOC-equivalent internal audit; achieved SLA of 99.95% for inference availability in production month 2.
- Owner: Solutions Engineering (Maya Singh)

6) Security FAQ for prospect conversations (short form)

Q: Can Redwood host customer data?
A: Yes — Hosted API stores minimal telemetry for operational purposes. For regulated data we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. For Private, data resides in your VPC/on-prem. See evidence packet: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/2026-soc2-summary.json

Q: How do you handle encryption and key management?
A: We support customer-managed keys (KMS integrations) and HSM-backed key stores in Private deployments. We provide key rotation guidance and documented procedures for audit.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access trails?
A: Yes — Audit logging is available for all Dedicated and Private customers with configurable retention. Standard retention 90 days; longer retention available as add-on.

Q: What certifications and third-party assessments do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness program; we provide redacted evidence packages under NDA.

Q: How do you protect against model leakage and prompt data exposure?
A: We provide per-route privacy controls, optional request stripping, and KV cache isolation. In Private deployments, the customer controls storage and retention.

7) Pilot & POC checklist (recommended 6-week pilot)

Week 0: Kickoff & success metrics (define latency p95 target, cost baseline, quality eval prompts)
Week 1: Provision test account / dedicated pool or Private staging, integrate SDKs, sample workload ingestion
Week 2: Baseline measurements (latency, token counts, error rates) + initial tuning (batching, cache)
Week 3: Run regression evals and quality checks; adjust model variant if necessary
Week 4: Scale throughput to expected production level; monitor SLOs; validate observability dashboards
Week 5: Knowledge transfer, runbook handoff, compliance evidence delivery
Week 6: Exec review & next-step proposal (commit sizing + commercial terms)

POC success criteria (example):
- p95 latency <= 500ms for 90% of traffic
- Inference unit cost reduction >= 30% vs baseline
- Quality regression delta <= 2% on agreed prompt set

- Typical p50/p95 numbers observed (internal, representative):
  - redwood-chat-2k (Hosted, medium region): p50 85ms, p95 420ms for single-turn chat (context 2k).
  - quantized variants on Dedicated: 1.8–2.6x throughput improvement vs fp16 in our microbenchmarks.

Appendix B — Common rebuttal scripts (short)
- "We already have a self-hosted solution": "Understood — many teams start there. We typically win where customers need predictable SLAs, lower ops cost, or a clear migration path from hosted to private. Let's run a 6-week cost and reliability pilot to measure TCO."
